items.stem: Which of these is the STRONGEST password?
Where should your DT work live so you can open it anywhere, even at home?
options: Only on the computer you made it on

items.stem: What does a padlock on a lesson tile mean?
options: Not unlocked yet — your teacher controls it

items.stem: What do your C2k username and password actually let you do?
options: Use one specific computer only — yours
Log into any school machine and reach your own files
They're the same as a home email account
Share your login safely, since it's just for school

items.stem: A 'Digital Citizen' is someone who mainly…
options: Uses digital tech safely and responsibly in everyday life

items.stem: Your account gets logged in on the wrong machine by accident. What should you do?
Who can see your Mission Control badge scores?
options: The whole class on a leaderboard

items.stem: Which of these is an INPUT?
What do you need before 'show icon' will ever run?
options: Nothing — it runs automatically like a slideshow
A trigger event, like 'on button A pressed'
A forever block on its own

items.stem: In Rung 4 you built: on shake → show string → pause (ms) 1000 → clear screen. What happens if you DELETE the pause block?
options: The message wipes the instant it finishes — too fast to be sure you saw it
The message stays on the screen forever
The micro:bit refuses to run the program
The message scrolls twice as fast

items.stem: Button A is wired to a heart icon. What happens if you press button B instead?
options: Nothing — B has no code attached to it

items.stem: score = 3. What does this actually mean?
options: A box named 'score' currently holds 3 — and it can change
Score must be spelled with 3 letters

items.stem: What does 'change score by 1' do to a score that's currently 4?
Why does pressing B set score back to 0 before a new game starts?
options: So counting starts fresh — the last game's score can't leak in
Because zero is the default colour
The micro:bit won't start a new game without it

items.stem: Is a score variable storing a number or a word?
What does 'if score > highScore' actually check?
options: It asks a question: is score bigger than highScore right now?

items.stem: A sprite's script never runs when the green flag is clicked. What's the MOST likely reason?
options: There's no green-flag hat block on that script
The code is at the bottom of the workspace

items.stem: Two sprites both need to react to the same key press. What do you need?
options: Just one script — sprites share code automatically
To press the key twice as hard

items.stem: A block inside a forever loop runs…
options: Again and again until the program stops

items.stem: 'Change score by 0' vs 'change score by 1' — what's the real-world difference?
options: No difference — both count as scoring
By 0 the score sits stuck; by 1 it actually counts

items.stem: Does the order of blocks matter in Scratch?
options: No — order never matters in Scratch
Yes — within a script, steps run top to bottom, so order changes what happens

items.stem: In an if/else block, what happens when the condition is FALSE?
'if score = 10' compared with 'set score to 10' — what's the difference?
options: One ASKS whether score is 10; the other MAKES it 10

items.stem: In Catch It, what should happen when the falling object is MISSED?
options: The score still goes up, just more slowly
The ELSE branch runs — lives go down instead of score going up

items.stem: On the Studio QA Desk, a test comes back with a CROSS. What does a real studio do next?
options: Record it as a tick anyway — it'll probably work on the day
Make the fix, then RUN THE SAME TEST AGAIN before recording a tick
Delete the game and start again from the kit
Skip that check — three ticks out of four is plenty

items.stem: You changed the backdrop and sprites but forgot the lives variable. Have you met the design brief?
options: No — looking finished isn't the same as working; the brief lists required features

items.stem: Your 'School' folder lives in your Google Drive. Where can you open it?
options: Any device where I sign in — school, home, even a phone
Only the computer where I first made it
Only when a teacher shares it back to me

items.stem: You typed an essay in Word Online and a story in Google Docs. Which is TRUE?
options: They live in two separate clouds — OneDrive and Google Drive
They're saved in the same place because it's one login
They swap between the clouds overnight
Only the Word one is really saved
